clue.text: Sweet woman's brought in having solid figure

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so the woman's word goes within the solid-figure word

parts.note: a cube is a solid figure, so having one is cubic
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A sweet woman is said to have a solid figure, like a compliment on her build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is the definition in its sense of angelic-looking; 'woman's' gives the pronoun, not a possessive noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sweet, innocent face is called angelic, like a little winged infant in a painting.

clue.text: Loud or quiet in loud old song

parts.note: f is forte, the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: the quiet word is placed in the middle of the loud-plus-song letters

parts.note: a lay is an archaic word for a ballad or song
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A musician asks whether a passage of an old song should be played loud or quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Loud' is the definition, in its sense of gaudy; the second is the musical forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: loud clothes or tastes are showy and ostentatious.

clue.text: Indicator of time passing no monarch will bear

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, as a bearer holds a load

explanation.surface: Something that marks time going by, with no king to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will bear' signals letters held within 'passinG NO MONarch'. 'passing' looks like part of the definition but supplies the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the upright pin on a sundial whose shadow tells the hour.

clue.text: Curious about old record for classification of complaints

indicators.note: the curious word goes around the old record, surrounding it

parts.note: a nosy person is curious about others' business
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone is curious about an old record used to classify complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' means illnesses, not grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: the branch of medicine that classifies diseases, here called complaints.

clue.text: Colour of imprisoned Yankee?

indicators.note: here of carries the sense 'made up of a Yankee imprisoned', the prison word wrapped round the Yankee letter

parts.note: imprisoned is read as 'in can', can being US slang for prison, so it gives the prison word
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about what colour an American prisoner might turn, or wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' really does two jobs: read as 'in can' (can = prison in US slang), it both supplies CAN and puts Y (Yankee) inside it; the question mark flags that liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a greenish-blue shade, one of the printer's primary inks.

clue.text: Fail always to avoid Indian food

parts.note: to bomb is to flop or fail badly
ay is a poetic word for always, as in for ay
to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: Someone always fails to steer clear of curry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'duck' here is no bird: it is a dried, salted fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dried fish (the bummalo) eaten as a relish in Indian cookery.

clue.text: Gold on border in the baroque landing area

indicators.note: the gold-and-border letters sit inside the rearranged three-letter word
baroque means extravagantly ornate, so the letters of the are twisted out of shape
in an across clue, on means placed after, so gold follows border

parts.note: a lip is the edge or rim of something
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gilded border within a baroque building marks where something lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' rearranges THE so that its last letter ends up at the end, around the gold-and-border letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a pad or site where helicopters take off and set down.

clue.text: Youngster carrying round items for washing machine?

indicators.note: the youngster word holds the round letter within it

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A boy carries a round of laundry to the washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: a batch of clothes put in to wash at one time is called this.

clue.text: Old lady leaving the least revealing garment

indicators.note: the old lady departs from the least word, so her letters are taken away

parts.note: the minimum is the least possible amount
mum is a mother, informally one's old lady

explanation.surface: An old woman abandons the least revealing outfit for something daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes MUM from the end of MINIMUM. 'least revealing' reads as one phrase, but 'revealing garment' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: a very short skirt, shortened from miniskirt.

clue.text: Large individual's double helping of seconds after eating out

indicators.note: the doubled letters come after the rearranged ones
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of eating are rearranged
a double helping gives two of the same thing

explanation.surface: A big person has two helpings of seconds after eating out at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EATING as GIANTE. 'seconds' tempts as more food but is the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female giant, an individual of great size.

clue.text: Not pro musicians in unwanted traffic

parts.note: contra means against, the opposite of pro
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Amateur musicians playing in a nuisance stream of road traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not pro' suggests amateur, but gives CONTRA (against). 'traffic' means trade, not cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: smuggled goods, trade the authorities do not allow.

clue.text: Scream from Port Talbot's leader

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cry heard from the head of Port Talbot, a Welsh steel town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port Talbot' looks like one name, but 'Port' alone gives RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a very funny person or thing is called a scream or this.

clue.text: Confused group from hotel in big motorway collision

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: the hotel letter is placed in the motorway-and-collision letters

parts.note: a smash is a crash
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A confused group emerges from a hotel near a big motorway pile-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's main motorway north from London, its digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a jumble or muddle, a confused collection of things.

clue.text: Great place to pee, in regularly scrubbed urinal

indicators.note: the to-and-pee letters go inside the letters kept from urinal
every other letter is scrubbed away, keeping a regular pattern

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone praises a scrubbed urinal as a great place to relieve oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly scrubbed' keeps U, I, A from URINAL; 'in' puts TO+P after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic synonym: an imagined perfect society, the greatest place there could be.

clue.text: Times to absorb fruit's goodness

indicators.note: the times word takes in the fruit letters

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in four by three
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The newspaper urges readers to absorb fruit's nutritional goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' is the exclamation, not virtue or nutrition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'my goodness!'

clue.text: Denying taking drugs along with official

indicators.note: the drugs word goes along with the official word, joined after it

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a match official
using is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: An athlete denies taking drugs, and an official sides with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: declining or withholding something is denying it.

clue.text: Hungary's borders separately within reach

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the borders of a word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: taking the two border letters separately means listing them one and the other, so the joining word goes between them

explanation.surface: Hungary's frontiers lie each within easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The borders of HUNGARY, taken separately, are 'H and Y', spelt in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something close by and convenient is at hand.

clue.text: Pope devotee pens brief quote about Shelley?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the devotee word holds the other letters

parts.note: a Romanist is an adherent of the Roman Catholic Church, led by the Pope

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the shortened quote is read backwards
brief means cut short, so the quote word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A papal devotee writes a short quotation about the poet Shelley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' tempts as the poet Alexander Pope, but the devotee is a follower of the Pope in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Percy Bysshe Shelley was a leading poet of the Romantic movement.

clue.text: Caution after river's edge shows evidence of deposits

indicators.note: in a down clue, after means the caution word follows the other

parts.note: a bank is the side of a river
to book a player is to caution him officially, in football

explanation.surface: A caution after spotting silt at the river's edge reveals deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposits' looks geological beside the river, but means money paid into a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a passbook records money paid into an account, so it shows deposits made.

clue.text: Beaten team reproaching person doing shooting

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a defeat, the team berates the person shooting at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges TEAM REPROACHING. 'shooting' means filming, not taking shots at goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the director of photography, who handles the camera when a film is shot.

clue.text: Movement in E flat's merry

indicators.note: movement in the letters shifts them about, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A symphony movement written in E flat has a merry character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement in' rearranges E FLATS. 'Movement' reads as part of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to a feast or holiday, so joyous and festive.

clue.text: What might bore everyone listening

indicators.note: to people listening, the everyone word is heard as the answer

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Something that might bore everyone who listens to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' means drill a hole, not weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Wasted time in school, getting U

parts.note: wasted and high are both slang for intoxicated on drugs
a class is a lesson, a period of time in school

explanation.surface: A pupil wastes time in school yet still gets a U grade.
explanation.walkthrough: U is not a failing grade here: it is the British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Convention: U stands for upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U speech.

clue.text: Harmful to wipe out evidence of debts? That's about right

indicators.note: the other letters go about the right letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to delete is to wipe out
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts owed

explanation.surface: Destroying proof of what you owe is harmful, but is it right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' just links the wordplay; the question mark flags IOUs as a playful sort of evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: causing damage or injury, as with deleterious effects on health.

clue.text: Real idiot broadcast declaration of opinion

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A real fool goes on air to air his views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges REAL IDIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a newspaper's leading article stating the paper's own view.

clue.text: Pudding's eaten along with last of sugar flakes on top

indicators.note: the pudding has eaten the other letters, taking them inside

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
and means along with

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pudding is eaten with sugar flakes sprinkled on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding's' is 'pudding has', not a possessive; duff is a British boiled suet pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: scaly skin flakes from the scalp, found on top of the head.

clue.text: Church office quick to engage secretary

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the quick word takes the secretary inside

parts.note: pacy means fast
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A church office moves quickly to hire a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: PACY is British for fast-moving, used of footballers and thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the position held by the Pope, head of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Love revolutionary kind of film stars

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written O

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the film word is read backwards

parts.note: noir is a genre of dark crime film

explanation.surface: The stars of a revolutionary film that someone loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' tempts as film actors, but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Hunter, a prominent constellation of stars.

clue.text: Half-cut people murmur

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the first half of the word

parts.note: humans are people

explanation.surface: Drunken people mumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' means drunk, but here keeps the first half of HUMANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a low continuous sound, such as a murmur of voices.
